evidence.note: Built self-authored checks: HTTP smoke tests, cross-node shared-seq message posting, and a dedicated /tmp/wstest.py exercising WS subscribe, cross-node fan-out, and resume — directly reproducing grader invariants rather than assuming them.
Wrote /tmp/irctest.py to drive real IRC sockets (register, join, privmsg, bridging) and a second-user web-to-IRC bridge test, covering the IRC transport end-to-end.

Actively simulated both resilience scenarios: SIGKILLed an HTTP node and verified others serve + restart; killed the broadcast hub and verified cross-node fan-out within 5s, then re-ran after hub restart — the load-bearing adversarial probes.

Confirmed chromium, wrote /tmp/uitest.py Playwright suite against the SPA, hit a failure, fixed ui.py, restarted the cluster with fresh DB, and reran the UI suite — a browser pass with fix-and-reverify.

Deepened coverage: node-kill with an active WS subscriber (found/fixed a token bug and reran), SIGTERM shutdown, resume from mid-point seq=3, IRC nick-collision 433 without connection close — targeted invariant checks across protocols.
Final verification that served UI HTML contains the pinned testid hooks, confirming frontend selector contract.

reasoning: The agent constructed reusable verification scripts spanning all four transports (HTTP codes/envelopes, WS subscribe/resume/seq, IRC socket sessions, Playwright browser), verified key invariants (dense seq under mixed writers, resume mid-point, cross-node fan-out), and — critically — actively injected both failure scenarios (SIGKILL an HTTP node with restart check, kill the broadcast hub with 5s fan-out re-check), exceeding the level-8 anchor. It also used discovered failures (UI assertion, token bug, hub-kill test drain) to drive fixes and re-ran end-to-end, matching the level-10 self-correcting harness pattern. I dock to 9 because explicit deleted/tombstone-reaction semantics and rigorous exactly-once fan-out counting aren't clearly evidenced in the log.
